newsitem.title: UK: Dunblane parents make film to mark massacre.
newsitem.headline: Dunblane parents make film to mark massacre.

text.p: The parents of 16 children massacred in Scotland last year released a film on Tuesday to commemorate their children.
The film, to be broadcast in Britain on March 12, shows interviews with some of the bereaved parents along with photographs and videos of the victims.
"We decided to make this film to show how sadness and pain can be mixed...with joy," said David Scott, whose daughter Hannah was killed.

Sixteen five- and six-year-olds and a teacher were shot dead when deranged Thomas Hamilton burst into their gym on March 13 last year. Twelve children and another teacher were injured. Hamilton killed himself.

"We decided to make this film to show how, in tragic circumstances, we can be positive, how difficult it is day to day, how all of our priorities have changed, how we support each other...and how the children and (teacher) Gwen (Mayor) live on," the parents said in a collective statement.
Along with the interviews with 14 of the parents, the film shows them playing with surviving siblings and visiting their children's graves.
They all agreed they wanted to remember their lost children.
"Emily ...used to drive me nuts a lot of the time," Les Morton said of his daughter. "But I tell you what -- I wish I was home and tired and Emily was irritating me right now."

The massacre transformed the tiny Scottish cathedral city. Hundreds of reporters from around the world descended on the town, while well-wishers sent flowers and toys that lined the pavements outside Dunblane Primary School for weeks.
"It's just amazing to think the whole of the world had been touched," Barbara Dunn, whose daughter Charlotte was killed, said in the film.
"You can't believe that so many people are thinking of us."
